'''Dwight Buycks''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|b|aɪ|k|s}} {{respell|BYKES}}; born March 6, 1989) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Kalleh Mazandaran BC|Kalleh Mazandaran]] of the [[Iranian Basketball Super League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Indian Hills Community College|Indian Hills Warriors]] and [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette Golden Eagles]].

==High school career==
Buycks attended [[Bay View High School (Milwaukee, WI)|Bay View High School]] in [[Milwaukee, Wisconsin]]. He was a four-year starter on the basketball team and finished his career with 1,312 points. He was the first player in school history to reach 1,000 points. He was named to the All-League Team all four years and the [[Associated Press|AP]] and Coaches All-State Team in his senior year. He was voted the top [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] player in the state and led his team to the state championship.<ref name=bio>{{Cite web |url=http://www.gomarquette.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/buycks_dwight00.html |title=Dwight Buycks Bio |access-date=2013-07-09 |archive-date=2013-09-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130905053020/http://www.gomarquette.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/buycks_dwight00.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==College career==

===Junior college===
Buycks attended [[Indian Hills Community College]] for the 2007–08 and 2008–09 seasons. In his two years, he had 1,254 points, the third most in school history. During his time there, his team was 58–13. They also won a conference tournament championship and made a national tournament appearance. He was on the first team All-Region Team in both his seasons. He was also a First Team [[National Junior College Athletic Association|NJCAA]] All-American selection in his sophomore year. His team was ranked in the top five all year and were second in the final poll. They finished sixth in the national tournament.

===2009–10 season===
During the [[2009–10 Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball team|2009–10 season]], Buycks was mainly [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette's]] sixth man. During the season, he started 11 games and averaged 24 minutes per game. He averaged 6.3 points per game and 3 rebounds per game while earning his first letter.

===2010–11 season===
In his senior season, Buycks had an increased role, averaging 28.1 minutes per game. In 36 games, he averaged 8.8 points, 3.1 rebounds, 3.4 assists and 1.1 steals per game.<ref>[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/dwight-buycks-1.html Dwight Buycks Stats]</ref>

==Professional career==

===2011–12 season===
Buycks went undrafted in the [[2011 NBA draft]]. In November 2011, he was acquired by the [[Tulsa 66ers]] of the [[NBA G League|NBA Development League]] (D-League).<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/tulsa/tulsa_66ers_add_10_players___2011_11_03.html TULSA 66ERS ADD 10 PLAYERS IN 2011 NBA D-LEAGUE DRAFT] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131217165749/http://www.nba.com/dleague/tulsa/tulsa_66ers_add_10_players___2011_11_03.html |date=2013-12-17 }}</ref> On December 11, 2011, he signed with the [[Phoenix Suns]]. However, he was later waived by the Suns on December 19, 2011. He then returned to the 66ers. In April 2012, following the conclusion of the D-League season, he signed with [[BC Oostende|Oostende]] of Belgium for the remainder of the [[2011–12 Ethias League]] season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/belgium/37810/telenet-oostende-tabs-dwight-buycks.html Telenet Oostende tabs Dwight Buycks]</ref>

===2012–13 season===
In July 2012, Buycks joined the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] for the Orlando [[NBA Summer League|Summer League]] and the [[San Antonio Spurs]] for the Las Vegas Summer League. In August 2012, he signed with [[BCM Gravelines]] of France for the 2012–13 season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/france/42224/gravelines-dunkerque-put-dwight-buycks-at-point.html Gravelines-Dunkerque put Dwight Buycks at point]</ref>

===2013–14 season===
In July 2013, Buycks re-joined the Oklahoma City Thunder for the [[2013 NBA Summer League|2013 Orlando Summer League]]. On July 16, 2013, he signed a two-year deal with the [[Toronto Raptors]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/raptors-sign-guard-dwight-buycks/ |title=Raptors Sign Free-Agent Guard Dwight Buycks |access-date=2013-07-17 |archive-date=2013-07-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130721002726/http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/raptors-sign-guard-dwight-buycks/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> after playing well for them in the Las Vegas Summer League. On January 3, 2014, he was assigned to the [[Bakersfield Jam]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/buycks-010314/ |title=Buycks Assigned To Bakersfield Jam |access-date=2014-01-05 |archive-date=2014-01-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140105090008/http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/buycks-010314/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> On January 13, 2014, he was recalled by the Raptors.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/buycks-recalled-from-bakersfield-jam/ |title=Buycks Recalled From Bakersfield Jam |access-date=2014-01-14 |archive-date=2014-01-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140115052620/http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/buycks-recalled-from-bakersfield-jam/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> On March 5, 2014, he was reassigned to the Jam.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/buycks-bakersfield-jam-030514/ |title=Buycks Reassigned To Bakersfield Jam |access-date=2014-03-06 |archive-date=2014-03-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140306071214/http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/buycks-bakersfield-jam-030514/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> On March 9, 2014, he was recalled by the Raptors.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/buycks-recalled-from-bakersfield-jam-2/ |title=Buycks Recalled From Bakersfield Jam |access-date=2014-03-10 |archive-date=2014-03-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140310183125/http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/buycks-recalled-from-bakersfield-jam-2/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===2014–15 season===
On July 19, 2014, Buycks was waived by the Toronto Raptors.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/128155/raptors-request-waivers-on-dwight-buycks-and-diante-garrett.html |title=Raptors request waivers on Dwight Buycks and Diante Garrett |access-date=2014-07-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170914220551/http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/128155/raptors-request-waivers-on-dwight-buycks-and-diante-garrett.html |archive-date=2017-09-14 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Six days later, he signed a one-year deal with [[Valencia Basket]] of the [[Liga ACB]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/128905/valencia-basket-announces-dwight-buycks.html Valencia Basket announces Dwight Buycks]</ref><ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/138660 Valencia Basket brings on Buycks]</ref> On November 7, 2014, he parted ways with Valencia after five Spanish League games and three [[EuroLeague]] games.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/140349/valencia-and-dwight-buycks-part-ways.html Valencia and Dwight Buycks part ways]</ref> Head coach [[Velimir Perasović]] said that Buycks' release was consensual and that Valencia wanted to part ways with him due to bad results. Perasović pointed to himself as the possible reason as to why Buycks did not fit in with the team.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.abc.es/agencias/noticia.asp?noticia=1714943 | title=Perasovic: Esperábamos mucho Buycks, no ha sido así y puede que sea por mí | work=ABC.es | date=November 7, 2014 | access-date=November 8, 2014|language=es}}</ref>

On December 16, 2014, Buycks signed with [[Tianjin Ronggang]] for the rest of the [[2014–15 CBA season]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/145028/dwight-buycks-signs-with-tianjin-steel.html Dwight Buycks signs with TianJin Steel]</ref> Following the conclusion of the CBA season, he returned to the United States, and on March 4, he was acquired by the [[Oklahoma City Blue]] of the NBA Development League.<ref>[http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4933728 Blue Acquires Dwight Buycks]</ref> On April 3, he signed a 10-day contract with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] to help the team deal with numerous injuries. The Lakers had to use an NBA hardship exemption in order to sign him as he made their roster stand at 16, one over the allowed limited of 15.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/150403_dwight_buycks | title=Lakers Sign Dwight Buycks to 10-Day Contract | work=NBA.com | date=April 3, 2015 | access-date=April 3, 2015}}</ref> The Lakers parted ways with Buycks on April 13 after he suffered a broken right hand in the team's loss to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] the previous night.<ref>[http://www.hoopsrumors.com/2015/04/lakers-planned-buycks.html Lakers Planned To Re-Sign Buycks Before Injury]</ref>

===2015–16 season===
In July 2015, Buycks re-joined the Los Angeles Lakers for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/15_summerLeagueRoster Lakers Announce 2015 Summer League Roster]</ref> On September 24, 2015, he signed with the [[Fujian Sturgeons]] for the [[2015–16 CBA season]], returning to China for a second stint.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/176719/dwight-buycks-signs-in-china-with-fujian.html Dwight Buycks signs in China with Fujian]</ref> In 38 games for Fujian, he averaged 25.6 points, 6.4 rebounds, 5.7 assists and 2.2 steals per game.

Following the conclusion of the CBA season, Buycks returned to the United States, where on February 27, he was re-acquired by the Oklahoma City Blue.<ref>{{cite web|title=Blue Acquires Dwight Buycks|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/blue-acquires-dwight-buycks/n-5105153|access-date=November 14, 2015|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=February 27, 2016}}</ref> He made his season debut for the Blue that night in a 90–78 win over the [[Austin Spurs]], recording 14 points, five rebounds, five assists and two steals in 26 minutes.<ref>{{cite web|title=Blue Lock Down Spurs|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160227/AUSOKL/|access-date=February 27, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=February 27, 2016}}</ref>

===2016–17 season===
On August 7, 2016, Buycks re-signed with the [[Fujian Sturgeons]] for the 2016–17 CBA season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dwight Buycks agreed to terms with Fujian|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/208966/dwight-buycks-agreed-to-terms-with-fujian.html|access-date=August 8, 2016|work=Sportando.com|date=August 7, 2016}}</ref>

=== 2017–18 season ===
In July 2017, Buycks joined the [[Dallas Mavericks]] for the Orlando Summer League.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.scout.com/nba/mavericks/story/1788151-mavs-orlando-summer-league-roster-set|title=Mavs Orlando Summer League Roster Set|work=Scout.com|access-date=2017-07-11|language=en}}</ref> He helped lead them to the championship, scoring a team-leading 28 points in their overtime win over the Detroit Pistons.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-win-orlando-pro-summer-league/|title=Mavericks win Orlando Pro Summer League – Official Website of the Dallas Mavericks|date=2017-07-06|work=The Official Site of the Dallas Mavericks|access-date=2017-07-11|language=en-US}}</ref>

On September 12, 2017, Buycks signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Detroit Pistons. Under the terms of the deal, he will split time between the Pistons and their NBA G League affiliate, the Grand Rapids Drive.<ref>{{cite news|title=#Pistons have officially signed Dwight Buycks to a two-way contract.|url=https://twitter.com/detroitpistons/status/907688994208612352|access-date=September 14, 2017|work=Twitter.com|date=September 12, 2017}}</ref> Four months later, on January 12, 2018, Buycks' deal would be converted into a full, regular season deal.<ref>{{cite news|title=Rehab experience lends Jackson perspective; Pistons add Buycks for full season|url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/features/rehab-experience-lends-jackson-perspective-pistons-add-buycks-full-season|access-date=January 15, 2018|work=NBA.com|date=January 12, 2018}}</ref> He averaged 7.4 points and 2.0 assists per game. On July 7, 2018, he was waived by the Pistons.<ref>{{cite web|title=The #Pistons have requested waivers on guard Dwight Buycks.|url=https://twitter.com/DetroitPistons/status/1015714327582699521|website=Detroit Pistons on Twitter|access-date=July 9, 2018|date=July 7, 2018}}</ref>

=== 2018–19 season ===
In November 2018 Buycks signed with the Shenzhen Leopards for the 2018–19 CBA season. He averaged 20.5 points, 4.7 rebounds and 5.3 assists per game.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/international/players/dwight-buycks-1.html|title=Dwight Buycks International Stats|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en|access-date=2019-08-19}}</ref>

=== 2019–20 season ===
Buycks signed with [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]] on February 16, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Dwight Buycks signs with Olympiacos |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/dwight-buycks-signs-with-olympiacos/ |website=Sportando |access-date=February 16, 2020 |date=February 16, 2020 |last1=Lupo |first1=Nicola }}</ref>

=== 2020–21 season ===
On August 9, 2020, Buycks signed with [[Nanterre 92]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Dwight Buycks signs with Nanterre 92 |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/dwight-buycks-signs-with-nanterre-92/ |website=Sportando |access-date=August 9, 2020 |date=August 8, 2020 |last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref> In four games, he averaged 9.5 points, 1.3 rebounds and 3.3 assists per game. Buycks parted ways with the team on November 9.<ref>{{cite web |title=Buycks left Nanterre |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Eurocup/news/652496/Buycks-left-Nanterre |website=Eurobasket |access-date=November 9, 2020 |date=November 9, 2020}}</ref>

=== 2024–25 season ===
On September 15, 2024, Buycks signed with [[Kalleh Mazandaran BC|Kalleh Mazandaran]] of the [[Iranian Basketball Super League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Kalleh tabs Dwight Buycks |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Iran/news/891587/Kalleh-tabs-Dwight-Buycks |website=Eurobasket.com |access-date=11 November 2024 |date=15 September 2024}}</ref>
